clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old girl with unremarkable past medical history presented with 3 weeks of right-sided headache (described as 'heaviness' above the right eye) and horizontal binocular diplopia. She was initially misdiagnosed with migraines and treated with amitriptyline without improvement. An ophthalmologist diagnosed right cranial nerve VI palsy. Initial outpatient MRI brain with and without gadolinium was read as 'normal.' On hospital admission, she was afebrile with normal vital signs; physical examination confirmed impaired abduction of the right eye with esotropia, while vision, color vision, visual fields, and pupillary responses were normal. Comprehensive diagnostic workup was performed: CSF studies showed normal cell count, negative meningitis PCR, no growth on culture, normal AFP, no malignant cells, no oligoclonal bands, and normal ACE. Serum studies were negative for ANA, ANCA, anti-dsDNA, abnormal IgG subclasses, and infectious etiologies (cryptococcal antibodies, RPR, Lyme disease, mycoplasma, HIV, West Nile PCR), and serum protein electrophoresis was normal. These negative findings ruled out neoplastic processes (such as lymphoma) and systemic inflammatory or infectious etiologies. A repeat MRI brain and orbits with/without gadolinium obtained 11 days after the initial study revealed a possible cavernous sinus lesion, consistent with an inflammatory process. After multidisciplinary discussion involving neurology, ophthalmology, and hematology/oncology, the patient was treated with intravenous high-dose methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days, resulting in documented improvements in headaches, diplopia, and right eye abduction. She was discharged on a prolonged steroid taper with close ophthalmology follow-up. The diagnosis of Tolosa-Hunt syndrome (idiopathic inflammatory process) was concluded based on the clinical presentation of cranial nerve VI palsy with orbital/cavernous sinus involvement, negative workup for neoplastic and infectious etiologies, and dramatic response to corticosteroid therapy.
